subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a core shell-facing admin notification surface for connected Control UI sessions, fold it into the broader WebUI notification architecture, or keep shell-originated alerts outside core?
rationale: The requested behavior is absent, but adding it creates a new admin-scoped path from local scripts into connected UI clients and needs maintainer intent for authorization, targeting, payload shape, and interruption policy.

options.title: Design Core Notify Contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical CLI/Gateway/Control UI feature and require a typed admin event/RPC contract plus security controls before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into WebUI Notifications
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/20237 own the UI architecture and supersede this issue only after it explicitly covers shell/admin broadcast semantics.

options.title: Prefer Plugin Or External Delivery
options.body: Reject a core command and document the supported plugin, channel, Web Push, or node-notify path if maintainers decide shell alerts should not directly interrupt Control UI sessions.

recommendation.title: Design Core Notify Contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical CLI/Gateway/Control UI feature and require a typed admin event/RPC contract plus security controls before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses the current CLI, Gateway broadcast, Web Push, and Control UI surfaces where the strongest current-main routing evidence points.
